name: capp_multicell_2205
title: CAPP multiple-cell cavity in-depth study: sector-cell closed forms and optimal partition gap

citations.authors_short: J. Jeong, S. Youn, J. E. Kim

software.solver_type: 3D eigenmode, Monte Carlo over machining tolerance (100 samples per point)

geometry.description: N-cell cylinder (N = 2m) of radius Rc split by N/2 diametral partitions (N radial half-partitions) whose tips stop at distance Rg from the axis (centre gap). Table 2: closed form for the ideal sector (Rg = 0, thin partitions, long cavity). Figs. 5-6: COMSOL vs Rg/Rc with every dimension randomly perturbed by the stated tolerance

height.note: as-built: 215 mm for the Sec. 5 2/4/6-cell cavities; the Sec. 4 tuning-demo 6-cell cavity is a different build (220 mm)

tolerance.value: 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10 % random perturbation of radius of each cell, thickness and position of each partition

tuning_rods.value: none in Figs. 5-6; Fig. 2 uses eps = 10 rods, Rr/Rc ~ 0.1 (cylinder-equivalent)

conventions.form_factor_definition: C = |int B0.E dV|^2 / (int |B0|^2 dV int eps |E|^2 dV) (Eq. 2); volume of the |B0|^2 integral (full cylinder vs vacuum excluding partitions) not stated - see gaps
conventions.Q_definition: closed form Eqs. 5-6: Qc = (Rc/delta)/(1/Qbar + Rc/Lc); Table 2 "Q" = Qbar = Q delta/Rc normalized to m = 0; Qcyl = Q relative to an empty cylinder of the same frequency
conventions.notes: Fig. 5/6 C^2V^2Q is normalized to the ideal (0 % tolerance) cavity with Rg = 0 per Table 3 caption; Fig. 5 caption says "normalized to the ideally modeled cavity" - consistent only if the reference is the Rg = 0 ideal cavity (dashed curve = 1 at Rg = 0)

analytic_check.description: closed form (digitize/capp_sector_analytic.py) vs Table 2; Qbar = Q delta/Rc (fixed delta), Qcyl = Qbar * nu/nu0
findings: nu, Q, Qcyl, C of Table 2 reproduced to the printed 2 digits for all m
the printed Eq. 6 (1/Qbar) evaluates to our quadrature (m=1: Qbar = 0.5409)

digitized ideal (dashed) C at Rg -> 0: 2-cell 0.644-0.646, 4-cell 0.649, 6-cell 0.628 vs closed form 0.6440, 0.6493, 0.6341: 6-cell low by ~0.9% (7 px, beyond digitization error) - finite partition thickness/mesh in the COMSOL ideal model, unverified

measured_values.note: Fig. 7 (measured per-cell field strengths) and Sec. 5 C/C_ideal = 1.00/0.99/0.98 for 2/4/6 cells; not digitized. Build note (not an inconsistency): the Sec. 4 tuning demonstration uses a 6-cell cavity 110 mm ID x 220 mm, the Sec. 5 2/4/6-cell cavities are 110 mm ID x 215 mm - two different builds

gaps.parameter: Rc, height, partition thickness and copper sigma of the Fig. 5-6 models
gaps.proposal: results are normalized (C, C^2V^2Q relative to Rg = 0) so use the as-built 110 mm ID x 215 mm, 5 mm partitions, sigma = 5.8e7, and sweep partition thickness {thin, 5 mm} to see sensitivity; benchmark only the deterministic ideal (dashed) curves

gaps.issue: "dimensions allowed to randomly vary within 0.01-0.10 %" - distribution (uniform/normal) and which dimensions exactly are not specified
gaps.proposal: do not benchmark the MC points quantitatively; at most reproduce the trend with a uniform distribution on cell radii and partition positions

gaps.issue: "distance between the centre and the tip of a partition"; tip shape (square/rounded) not given

gaps.parameter: form-factor / volume convention for finite-thickness partitions
gaps.issue: Eq. 2 normalizes by int |B0|^2 dV over "the cavity volume" without saying whether the partitions are excluded. For the as-built 110 mm ID, 5 mm partitions the excluded area is ~5.8% (2-cell, one diametral plate, less the centre gap), ~11% (4-cell), ~16% (6-cell) of pi Rc^2 (about 7% for the 2-cell plate incl. typical Rg); C_vac = C_full/(1 - a). C^2 V^2 Q also depends on which V is used, and V_vac grows with Rg (shorter partitions), so the normalized Figs. 5-6 curves are convention-dependent at the few-% level
gaps.proposal: axionFEM must report C (and C^2 V^2 Q) both ways: V = full cylinder pi Rc^2 h and V = vacuum volume; the Table 2 closed form (zero-thickness partitions) is convention-free

inconsistencies.description: Eq. 7 (closed-form C) as printed gives C = 0 identically
inconsistencies.evidence: Eq. 7 (p.7) contains 1F2~(m/2+1; m/2+1, m+1; -chi_m1^2/4): with a = b1 it collapses to 0F1~(; m+1; -chi^2/4) ~ J_m(chi_m1) = 0 (mpmath: ~1e-32 for m = 0-4). With b1 = m/2 + 2 it gives 0.64402/0.64928/0.63411/0.61317 for m = 1-4 = our quadrature and Table 2; it still fails at m = 0 (0.5606 vs 0.6917; the sin(m phi) angular factor does not apply)
inconsistencies.proposal: do not use Eq. 7; capp_sector_analytic.py computes C by quadrature of the field solution (independent of Eq. 7)

inconsistencies.description: Table 3 4-cell optimum not on the simulated grid

inconsistencies.evidence: Fig. 5 caption: "normalized to those of the ideally modeled cavity"; Table 3 caption: "scan rates normalized to that for Rg = 0"
inconsistencies.proposal: normalize to the ideal Rg = 0 cavity (dashed curves start at 1.0)

inconsistencies.evidence: Sec. 5 "as can be seen in Fig. ??"; Fig. 3 caption labels the Q plot "(b)" twice
"# of partition" 0/2/4/6/8 equals the number of cells (half-partitions), not the number of diametral plates
inconsistencies.proposal: interpret as number of cells N = 2m

solver_class.reason: Table 2 = closed form (no FEM). Ideal gap curves: partitions full height, so the TM010-like mode is z-invariant: 2D scalar Helmholtz on the cross-section (not axisymmetric) or a 3D extrusion. Monte Carlo points: 3D, 100 solves per point

priority_reason: Table 2 is an exact analytic check; the ideal C(Rg) and C^2V^2Q(Rg) curves are deterministic but need unstated Rc/thickness and an unstated volume convention; the Fig. 6 dashed traces are truncated where they merge with the MC lines

readme_row.quantities: Tab 2 closed-form nu, Q, Qcyl, C vs m; Tab 3 optimal gap; Figs 5-6 C and C^2V^2Q vs Rg/Rc (MC + ideal curves)
readme_row.geometry_complete: yes (Tab 2); no (Figs 5-6: Rc, height, partition thickness, MC model)
